newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans to switch to unleaded petrol output.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans to switch to unleaded petrol output.

text.p: Bulgaria is negotiating a World Bank loan to help it switch to unleaded gasoline production by the year 2000 to meet European environmental standards, a deputy environment minister said on Tuesday.

Yoncho Pelovski said his ministry was negotiating with the World Bank for a loan of more than $40 million for the reconstruction of the country's biggest oil refinery Neftohim at the Black Sea port of Bourgas.
"I hope that we will sign an agreement with the World Bank next year so that Bulgaria will be able to solve its problem with petrol's leaded content by the year 2000," Pelovski said.
He said an environment ministry fund was prepared to help the project's implementation with $10 million and the refinery must fund the remaining $30 million.
"Under our project we need $82 million to reconstruct the Neftohim refinery in order to switch its production to unleaded gasoline," Pelovski told Reuters in an interview.
He said the project was aimed at raising the share of lead-free gasoline from 42 percent to 90 percent.
Demand for unleaded petrol in Bulgaria is expected to rise to 80 percent from the current 23 percent, officials said.

Neftohim, which annually processes about seven million tonnes of crude oil, supplies almost all of the oil products in the country, they said, adding that most of the refinery's 1.2 million tonnes annual output of gasoline is with lead content.
Apart from Neftohim, the country's main distributor Petrol needs time to reconstruct its filling stations for the new gasoline brands, officials said.

Bulgaria's many Soviet-made cars run on leaded petrol, though since the collapse of communism in 1989, wealthy businessmen have brought in luxury BMWs and Mercedes, creating a market for unleaded petrol.
